channel.title: The College Fix - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The College Fix (thecollegefix.com)

item.title: Chinese UMich researcher deported after smuggling in ‘noxious fungus’
item.description: Federal law enforcement deported a Chinese University of Michigan researcher who pled guilty for her role in bring in a crop fungus to the United States.

item.title: Lawmakers demand changes at U. Oklahoma after student’s Bible essay got a zero
item.description: Oklahoma lawmakers, frustrated by bias against conservatives and Christians in higher education, are threatening funding cuts to the University of Oklahoma.

item.title: Harvard professor who was ‘hunting rats’ near synagogue agrees to leave U.S.
item.description: Visiting Harvard Law professor Carlos Portugal Gouvea was arrested for shooting a pellet gun near a synagogue during Yom Kippur and has agreed to voluntarily deport to Brazil.

item.title: Hofstra U. black students: ‘fear’ and ‘frustration’ due to ‘multiple instances’ of racism this fall
item.description: Hofstra University black students express "fear" and "frustration" this fall due to multiple instances of racism, including graffiti incidents. Students report feeling unsafe and undervalued, with allegations of biased treatment from faculty. The Black Leaders Advocating for Change seek to address these ongoing racial issues, while university officials struggle with communication and transparency.

item.title: Yes, some professors ARE ‘out to get you’ – especially if you’re conservative
item.description: Samantha Fulnecky, a University of Oklahoma student, received a "zero" on a "reaction" paper from her transgender instructor, Mel Curth, sparking controversy. Critics argue her grading lacked justification and highlighted biases against conservative students, raising questions about how academia navigates differing political perspectives and fosters an environment of academic freedom.

item.title: George Washington U. scholars: ‘Rapid’ changes in U.S. policies are ‘harming its reputation’
item.description: George Washington University scholars argue that rapid shifts in U.S. policies are damaging the nation's global reputation. They note a stark divide between a sharply right-leaning GOP and a slowly leftward-moving Democratic Party, compounded by former President Trump's unpredictability, which has led to distrust abroad, particularly with China.

item.title: ‘Extraordinary intrusion’: Calif. professors demand halt to cybersecurity surveillance software
item.description: Tensions between UC faculty and administrators have been growing for more than a year over the controversy.

item.title: Wisconsin bill would forbid universities from raising tuition if they violate free speech rights
item.description: 'The penalties for violations prescribed in this bill would put the financial health of our universities at serious risk,' UW system official says.

item.title: Social work accreditor says colleges should teach students to ‘advocate for’ DEI
item.description: The Council on Social Work Education maintains accreditation standards emphasizing diversity, equity, and inclusion despite scrutiny from the Trump administration.

item.title: Mizzou professor accused of racism after she asked student for update on work
item.description: Mizzou Professor Michael Garcia lobbed racism allegations at a peer.
